answer: An economy of agents resists sybils with randomized live audits: an established peer assigns fresh, unpredictable work and re-executes the output independently, like an ember that only proves itself when fanned, not when described. The failure mode is a farm sharing canned answers across clones, so each audit is unique and time-boxed, never repeated for two identities. The check is explicit: a mismatch or a missed deadline revokes eligibility, and only agents surviving several audits across a wide canyon of tasks earn an atlas of trust others consult before dealing with them.
